correctness.rationale: The full proof defines the normalized row directions, independent finite sampling and the worst-initialization annealed factor with all quantifiers. It constructs the positive self-adjoint exact second-moment operator and its Gram eigenvalue representation, proves its spectral radius equals the worst-initialization exponent, and obtains the Rayleigh lower bound Gamma(p)>=[1+||sum p_i z_i||^2]/2. The closest-point planar circle geometry is proved for zero and positive distance. An isotropic distribution attains the bound exactly for every horizon when r=0; the two extreme directions at equal mass attain it otherwise, with an explicit all-initialization finite-time law and uniqueness. The bundled original script was actually run at its stated path; output VERIFY_OK 789 exact/geometry checks. Rational finite checks are not mistaken for the proof of infinite-horizon claims. The theorem explicitly excludes relaxed, noisy, and adaptively sampled variants.

It is the structural equality of the two optimum laws and the analytical all-frame formula.

originality.rationale: The primary 2014 works establish the one-step eigenvalue-bound sampling SDP and the exact annealed-rate SDP, respectively, and these are excluded from the novelty claim. Reading both full primary texts, including their mathematical optimization statements and their examples, did not uncover the planar doubled-angle distance formula, all-minimizer characterization, or the dimension-two coincidence of argmin sets. The general SDP defines an optimum implicitly but does not state or imply the explicit expression without the new Gram-Rayleigh lower bound and matching geometric construction. The earlier exponential convergence and later inconsistent-system papers do not claim the same specific result. Dedicated semantic and literal searches found no decisively covering publication. This is a self-review subject to the listed residual risk, not a global uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: The literal and semantic searches cannot prove worldwide uniqueness; an equivalent planar specialization in older optimal-design, frame, or projection-product literature may exist.

The general 2014 lifted SDP contains the present planar optimization as a mathematical special case, so its formulation must remain acknowledged prior art; the new claim is only its nontrivial explicit solution and coincidence statement.
The cited prior-result inventory is incomplete with respect to unpublished work; no unpublished priority or independent validation is claimed.

value.rationale: The arbitrary finite real planar Kaczmarz design problem is natural in tomographic projection and iterative linear solvers. Its optimal exact annealed convergence rate, all minimizers, and angular two/three-direction sparsity are determined in closed form without the general SDP. The proved equality between exact-rate optimizers and one-step-bound optimizers is a structural bridge between two previously distinct criteria, while their optimal numerical rates differ strictly for intermediate frame geometry. The finite examples demonstrate practical selection of two extreme directions, not an arbitrary unmotivated parameter slice. The claims do not assert a paper-sized or high-dimensional theorem.
